tests.note: no test was added. The checker's evidence is scripts/check_migrations.sh --self-test over a fixture pair, which is not a JUnit test because the checker is a gate script. Schema equivalence is covered by the existing integration tests: both services run hibernate ddl-auto=validate, so Hibernate compared every converted table against its entity mapping at context startup The pat failure is a race between PatUsageTracker's single-thread ludwigPatUsageExecutor, which re-reads and saves the row to record last use, and PatService.revoke, which the test calls immediately afterwards with no barrier between them.

unresolved: mvn clean install is not green: pat-spring-boot-starter's revokedTokenStopsWorking fails under full-reactor load. Schema identity rules the changelog format out as the mechanism, but 2 fails with the converted changelog against 1 pass with the original is too small a sample to call the conversion exonerated on timing grounds. This needs a decision: fix the race in PatService.revoke, or add a barrier in the test.

PatService.revoke has no tolerance for a concurrent PatUsageTracker write, which defeats the idempotency its own javadoc promises for incident response - an actively-abused token generates the most telemetry writes, so revocation is most likely to fail exactly when it matters most. Found during this change, out of scope, not fixed.

DATABASECHANGELOG.COMMENTS now holds a one-line summary where it previously held the full <comment> body: repeated --comment directives keep only the last line. The full rationale is in the file as -- prose. Accepted trade-off, design D5.
A non-PostgreSQL target now SKIPS changesets rather than failing, because every changeset declares dbms:postgresql. Safer than the partial schema it replaces, but it is a silent skip.
